positions.summary_short: Brown's campaign centres on a $3B second hospital breaking ground this fall, a $900M cancer care centre, and the TMU medical school that opened in 2025.
summary_bullets: $3 billion second hospital at the former Peel Memorial site — new inpatient tower, 24-hour emergency department, expanded outpatient services; construction begins fall 2026.
Estimated $900 million Comprehensive Cancer Care Centre at Brampton Civic Hospital ($3M approved for planning) to bring radiation and specialized cancer treatment closer to home.
$225 million TMU School of Medicine opened in 2025 — GTA's first new medical school in more than a century, with clinics connecting 14,000 residents to a family doctor.
positions.verbatim_quote: For too long Brampton didn't get its fair share. Today, we are witnessing the largest infrastructure investment in our city's history.
positions.source_title: Patrick Brown Files Nomination for Third Term as Mayor of Brampton (campaign launch release)

positions.summary_short: Brown backs the $2.8B Hazel McCallion LRT extension with a downtown tunnel and a $298M third transit operations facility.
summary_bullets: $2.8 billion Hazel McCallion LRT extension, including a tunnelled section into downtown Brampton — connecting to the regional rapid transit network while protecting/revitalizing the historic downtown.
$298 million Cadetta Johnston Transit Facility (Brampton Transit's third operations centre), under construction — expanding capacity and supporting future zero-emission bus growth.
positions.verbatim_quote: This once-in-a-generation investment will connect Brampton to the regional rapid transit network while protecting and revitalizing the city's historic downtown.
positions.source_title: Patrick Brown Files Nomination for Third Term as Mayor of Brampton (campaign launch release)

positions.summary_short: Brown highlights $1.7B in police facilities: a new 23 Division, modernized 22 Division, and a support facility housing the 9-1-1 centre.
summary_bullets: $1.7 billion in policing and public-safety facility investments: 23 Division (first new Peel Regional Police divisional building in nearly 40 years, northwest Brampton, ~500 personnel).
Sir Robert Peel Centre redevelopment and 22 Division modernization (~1,100 personnel).
New Operational Support Facility at 8100 Mississauga Road housing the 9-1-1 Communications Centre, Community Safety Operations Centre, data analytics and road safety services.
positions.verbatim_quote: A growing city needs a police service built for it.
positions.source_title: Patrick Brown Files Nomination for Third Term as Mayor of Brampton (campaign launch release)

positions.summary_short: Brown points to the $138M Riverwalk flood project and $45M downtown street rebuild as unlocking growth for ~17,700 residents and 24,000 jobs.
summary_bullets: $138 million Riverwalk Downtown Brampton Flood Protection Project (under construction): removes flood constraints along Etobicoke Creek, unlocking new development for ~17,700 new residents and nearly 24,000 jobs.
$45 million downtown revitalization: Main Street and Queen Street rebuilt from the sidewalks up, Garden Square and Ken Whillans Square redeveloped.
positions.verbatim_quote: These investments did not happen by accident. They happened because Brampton had a strong voice fighting for our fair share.
positions.source_title: Patrick Brown Files Nomination for Third Term as Mayor of Brampton (campaign launch release)

positions.summary_short: Brown's recreation plank includes the $16M Orangeville rail trail, the $160M Embleton community centre, and the $80M Howden recreation centre.
summary_bullets: $16 million Brampton-Orangeville Rail Trail: 14 km of former rail line becoming a walk/run/ride trail, joining a 51-km corridor into the Caledon hills.
$160 million Embleton Community Centre (under construction) — largest recreation investment in Brampton's history: aquatics, fitness, childcare, gathering areas.
$80 million Howden Recreation Centre and Library (construction begins soon): competition-sized gymnasium, new library branch, outdoor courts and play areas.
positions.verbatim_quote: Construction is underway on the largest recreation investment Brampton has ever made.
positions.source_title: Patrick Brown Files Nomination for Third Term as Mayor of Brampton (campaign launch release)

positions.summary_short: Tarriwal's 'Tell the Truth About the Tax Bill' priority promises transparency and respect for taxpayers' money, with detailed costing still pending.
summary_bullets: One of seven platform priorities: 'Tell the Truth About the Tax Bill' — framed around transparency and respect for taxpayers.
Core governing principles listed: set clear priorities, make responsible decisions, respect people's money, finish what you start.
Detailed costing and first-100-days commitments for each priority were 'still being written' at research time (2026-10-17).
positions.verbatim_quote: Brampton doesn't need more announcements. It needs leadership that follows through.
positions.source_title: Better Brampton — Paul Tarriwal for Mayor of Brampton (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Tarriwal lists public safety reaching business owners as a core priority, including dedicated community patrols with Peel Police.
summary_bullets: One of seven platform priorities: 'Safety That Reaches the Business Owner' — under the 'Stronger Communities: safer, cleaner, more connected' pillar.
Campaign's published commitments include 100 dedicated community patrols partnering with Peel Police on auto theft and illegal street racing (per platform preview materials).
Detailed costing and first-100-days commitments were 'still being written' at research time (2026-10-17).
positions.verbatim_quote: A Brampton resident. A father. A business professional. Not a career politician.
positions.source_title: Better Brampton — Paul Tarriwal for Mayor of Brampton (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Tarriwal committed to wind-row plowing so driveways aren't left blocked by plow-packed snow and ice, alongside a transit priority.
summary_bullets: Adds wind-row clearing to the platform: after the plow clears the road, the packed wall of snow and ice at the end of driveways would be cleared too — 'No more mountains of ice at the end of your driveway.'
One of seven platform priorities: 'Transit You Can Still Catch.'
Campaign promises each commitment will be published with the work shown: what it costs, who delivers it, when it starts and how residents can measure it.
positions.verbatim_quote: No more mountains of ice at the end of your driveway.
positions.source_title: New commitment: wind-row plowing (campaign update, Aug 25, 2026)

positions.summary_short: Somal runs on affordability and responsible spending: stable costs, less waste, and better accountability in city budgets.
summary_bullets: Affordability priority: 'Keeping life affordable for families' — focus on stable costs and reducing waste in city spending.
Responsible Spending priority: 'Better value for taxpayer money' — reduce waste and improve accountability in city budgets.
positions.verbatim_quote: I'm running for Mayor to improve city services, support families, and keep costs under control.
positions.source_title: Sandeep Somal For Mayor (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Somal's housing priority is building more homes faster by reducing approval delays.
summary_bullets: Housing & Growth priority: 'More homes, built faster' — reduce delays and unlock housing development.
positions.verbatim_quote: More homes, built faster.
positions.source_title: Sandeep Somal For Mayor (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Somal's safer-neighbourhoods plank focuses on upkeep, enforcement and local quality of life.
summary_bullets: Safer Neighbourhoods priority: 'Clean, well-maintained communities' — focus on upkeep, enforcement, and local quality of life.
positions.verbatim_quote: Clean, well-maintained communities.
positions.source_title: Sandeep Somal For Mayor (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Somal wants faster permits and service delivery, plus more affordable recreation and community spaces for kids and families.
summary_bullets: Efficient City Services priority: 'Fixing delays in city approvals' — speed up permits, applications, and service delivery.
Youth & Families priority: more affordable recreation, sports, and community spaces; better access to programs for kids.
positions.verbatim_quote: Let's make Brampton work better for the people who live here.
positions.source_title: Sandeep Somal For Mayor (campaign site)

positions.summary_short: Jackson's accountability posts question the city's debt schedule on the Innovation Centre and an $80M building/empty-office problem.
summary_bullets: 'The Case of the Missing Innovation Centre': questions a City debt repayment schedule showing $7M payments in 2026 and $12M from 2027, demanding answers on the Innovation Centre project.
'Brampton Has an $80 Million Building Problem — And an Empty Office Problem': challenges city spending on buildings and empty office space.
Platform goals: 'Strong Communities' (focused leadership, practical solutions), 'Connected City', 'Brighter Future'; holds live town halls every Tuesday 6-8 PM.
positions.verbatim_quote: This moment calls for focused leadership, practical solutions and the confidence to move our city forward.
positions.source_title: Wesley Jackson for Mayor (campaign site — news posts)

positions.summary_short: Gill's signature idea is a 'One problem, One owner' City Hall with a named owner per issue, plus reopening the cancelled forensic investigations.
summary_bullets: Centrepiece: turn City Hall into a 'One problem, One owner' institution — every issue delegated to a single named municipal official, empowered and held accountable; resident knows who owns their issue.

Would re-open the half-dozen forensic investigations into allegedly fraudulent procurements/hiring that a council majority launched and Brown cancelled in 2022; 'I'm publishing what they find and I'm serving the full four years.'

Says the current 311 system issues a ticket number with no updates on progress; his model would assign an official, publish a capital status report to council, and escalate to a departmental manager if unresolved — no restructuring or extra cost.
positions.verbatim_quote: Every problem that comes into City Hall gets one named person who owns it until it's solved. And the resident knows who that person is.
positions.source_title: Brampton mayoral candidate Prabh Gill has radical ideas to change City Hall (The Pointer)

positions.summary_short: Gill says $1.5-$1.6B in taxpayer-collected capital sits tied to unbuilt projects and attacks wasteful council travel.
summary_bullets: Says council staff confirmed $1.5-$1.6B in unspent capital tied to approved-but-unbuilt projects: 'The money was already collected from taxpayers for work that was somehow mismanaged... The projects never moved forward.'
Criticized a $19.4M internal loan from an emergency/rate-stabilization reserve to cover the operating budget, repaid via the hospital levy.
Attacked wasteful councillor travel ('flying to Taiwan, Portugal') costing tens of thousands with no benefit: 'with no investment to show for it, that's wasteful spending.'
positions.verbatim_quote: The City has collected somewhere between $1.5 and $1.6 billion from residents for capital projects that never got built. There's no transparency, no accountability.
positions.source_title: Brampton mayoral candidate Prabh Gill has radical ideas to change City Hall (The Pointer)

positions.summary_short: Gill demands answers on the stalled Peel Memorial hospital expansion and the city's $125M local-share commitment.
summary_bullets: Demands accountability on the stalled Peel Memorial Phase 2 expansion (stalled nearly a decade, final cost unknown); the City has committed $125M as its local share.
Says Brown never established a funding mechanism for the local share while demanding tax freezes.
Frames the mayor's responsibility as beginning 'the moment the city takes a dollar from residents' and ending only 'when the doors open.'
positions.verbatim_quote: The province funds it, Infrastructure Ontario procures it, and [William] Osler runs it. But the mayor's responsibility starts the moment the city takes a dollar from residents for it, and it does not end until the doors open.
positions.source_title: Brampton mayoral candidate Prabh Gill has radical ideas to change City Hall (The Pointer)

positions.summary_short: Gill calls the $11M closed-session Argo on-demand transit deal a 'backdoor deal' approved while transit service was cut.
summary_bullets: Attacked the $11M deal with private company Argo for on-demand transit, approved in a closed-session vote in April 2025 while Brampton Transit service was being cut and the transit union was bargaining.
Said no public information exists on the Argo agreement details after an FOI produced only scheduling emails and a redacted draft report.
positions.verbatim_quote: Instead of strengthening it, we're bringing...a backdoor deal with a private company.
positions.source_title: Brampton mayoral candidate Prabh Gill has radical ideas to change City Hall (The Pointer)

positions.summary_short: Gill wants to attract skilled trades to Brampton as Stellantis retools, saying supply decisions for the next decade are up for grabs.
summary_bullets: Stressed bringing more skilled trade workers to Brampton as the Stellantis auto plant retools: 'every supply decision for the next decade is up for grabs.'
Accused Brown of being too busy planning his next political move to help Brampton's 3,000 Stellantis workers; vowed never to use Brampton as a 'stepping stone.'
positions.verbatim_quote: The auto plant is retooling, and every supply decision for the next decade is up for grabs.
positions.source_title: Brampton mayoral candidate Prabh Gill has radical ideas to change City Hall (The Pointer)

positions.summary_short: Bhatt would put property-tax restraint first via a department-by-department spending review, plus relief/rebate options for seniors and hard-hit households.
summary_bullets: Make property-tax restraint a priority: lead a serious spending review, asking every department to separate essential services from expenditures that can be delayed, reduced or eliminated — before asking taxpayers for more.
Explore legally available relief and rebate programs for seniors and other qualifying households facing hardship.

Acknowledges City Hall can't solve inflation or set interest rates, but must do everything within its authority to keep costs down and advocate for residents when senior-government decisions affect them.
positions.verbatim_quote: Brampton doesn't need City Hall to make life more complicated. It needs municipal leadership that protects taxpayers, respects homeowners, supports businesses and remembers that behind every tax bill is a family working hard to pay it.
positions.source_title: My Home, My Brampton, My Sanctuary: Putting Money Back in Bramptonians' Pockets (guest column by the candidate, GTA Chronicle)

positions.summary_short: Bhatt would replace rental licensing with a simpler Occupancy C.A.R.E. safety model and accelerate affordable housing on City-owned land.
summary_bullets: Replace the Residential Rental Licensing framework with 'Occupancy C.A.R.E.' — a simpler, resident-friendly approach focused on legitimate health, fire and building-safety requirements.

Says responsible homeowners shouldn't be burdened by overlapping rules, paperwork and administrative requirements; overcrowding, dangerous construction and serious fire-code violations still can't be ignored.

Support accelerating appropriate affordable-housing projects on suitable City-owned lands, working with other governments and community organizations; strengthen partnerships with food banks and co-ops for food security.
positions.verbatim_quote: Your home should be your sanctuary, not a source of unnecessary fear or administrative stress.
positions.source_title: My Home, My Brampton, My Sanctuary: Putting Money Back in Bramptonians' Pockets (guest column by the candidate, GTA Chronicle)

positions.summary_short: Bhatt would use the mayor's office to press the province to end postal-code-based auto insurance rating that punishes Brampton drivers.
summary_bullets: Use the mayor's office to press the Ontario government and regulators for action on auto insurance affordability.
Target geographic/postal-code-based insurance rating: Brampton drivers shouldn't face unfairly high premiums 'simply because of where they live.'
Auto insurance is provincially regulated, but says the mayor should be a strong advocate for residents on it.
positions.verbatim_quote: The Mayor of Brampton should be a strong advocate for residents on an issue that has such a significant impact on household budgets.
positions.source_title: My Home, My Brampton, My Sanctuary: Putting Money Back in Bramptonians' Pockets (guest column by the candidate, GTA Chronicle)

positions.summary_short: Bhatt would cut city licensing and business fees 30-50% for small businesses and home-based entrepreneurs.
summary_bullets: Comprehensive review of City licensing and business fees, targeting 30-50% reductions for small businesses and home-based entrepreneurs 'where financially and legally feasible.'
Says municipal government should remove barriers to entrepreneurship, not add costs for people building businesses and creating jobs; keep necessary health, safety and consumer protections.
positions.verbatim_quote: Small businesses, personal-service operators and home-based entrepreneurs create jobs and keep money circulating in our community.
positions.source_title: My Home, My Brampton, My Sanctuary: Putting Money Back in Bramptonians' Pockets (guest column by the candidate, GTA Chronicle)

positions.summary_short: Bhatt wants significantly cheaper Brampton Transit passes for students and seniors, framing transit as an affordability policy.
summary_bullets: Make affordable, efficient public transit a major priority: pursue significantly cheaper Brampton Transit passes, particularly for students and seniors.
Frames transit as affordability policy: affordable transit could reduce pressure on families to maintain multiple vehicles, cutting insurance, fuel and maintenance costs.
Work with Council and other governments on transit affordability for residents who depend heavily on public transportation.
positions.verbatim_quote: Better transit is not simply a transportation policy; it can also be an affordability policy.
positions.source_title: My Home, My Brampton, My Sanctuary: Putting Money Back in Bramptonians' Pockets (guest column by the candidate, GTA Chronicle)
